project_type: Prompt-based AI adoption and process documentation lab
one_sentence_concept: A lightweight lab that helps non-technical teams learn process thinking, choose the right mapping perspective, map real workflows, and store process knowledge as portable assets before adopting AI or automation.
core_thesis: AI adoption starts with process clarity. Teams do not need to become BPMN professionals, but they need enough process literacy to understand work before they automate it.

strategic_positioning.bridge_work_fit: This lab fits Bridge Work as a practical tool for AI Adoption Architecture, governance-aware transformation, process literacy, and operational readiness.
strategic_positioning.main_message: Map the work. Then adopt the tool.
strategic_positioning.supporting_message: Process knowledge should survive the tool. That is part of exit strategy.
strategic_positioning.anti_pattern: Do not automate chaos. Do not build AI workflows on undocumented, poorly understood processes.
target_audience: teams preparing automation or AI use cases

product_narrative.short_version: Learn the symbols with Pietro. Choose the lens with Carla. Map the real work with the Sparring Partner. Store the knowledge with the Librarian.
product_narrative.expanded_version: The lab starts with playful BPMN literacy, then teaches the hardest part of process mapping: choosing the right perspective. Once the perspective is clear, the user maps a real workflow and stores the result as portable organisational knowledge.

learning_arc.name: Learn
learning_arc.purpose: Teach the beginner process language through a gamified pizza metaphor.

learning_arc.name: Choose
learning_arc.purpose: Help the user choose the right process, mapping goal, boundary and perspective.

learning_arc.name: Map
learning_arc.purpose: Turn a messy real workflow into a structured process map with AI opportunities and governance questions.

learning_arc.name: Store
learning_arc.purpose: Turn the map into portable process documentation: Markdown, Mermaid and JSON metadata.

key_principles.meaning: A useful process map does not need to be perfect BPMN. It needs to be true enough for the people doing the work.
Map the real process before designing the ideal process or automation.
The same process can be mapped through different lenses. Choose the lens before drawing.
One diagram should not show user experience, worker tasks, data flow, system architecture, governance and automation logic all at once.
Use BPMN as a thinking language, not as a certification exercise.
Use Mermaid for lightweight, text-based process diagrams that can render in chat, documentation systems or a viewer.
If the process only lives inside one AI tool or vendor UI, the organisation is locked in. Portable process assets preserve optionality.

recommended_elements.plain_language: Who owns or performs the work

labeling_rules.tasks: Use Verb + Noun, for example: Review invoice, Approve request, Send confirmation.
labeling_rules.events: Use Noun + State, for example: Application received, Request completed, Invoice rejected.
labeling_rules.decisions: Use clear questions, for example: Is request complete?

pietro_pizzaiolo.name: Pietro Pizzaiolo
pietro_pizzaiolo.tagline: Learn the symbols. BPMN through pizza.
pietro_pizzaiolo.purpose: Teach beginner process literacy through a playful, gamified metaphor.
pietro_pizzaiolo.user_start_signal: I am new to process mapping.
pietro_pizzaiolo.handoff_message: You now know how maps are drawn. Next, we need to choose what kind of map we need. A process map is not neutral. It is a view.

kaleidoskop_carla.name: Kaleidoskop Carla
kaleidoskop_carla.metaphor: Kaleidoscope: the same object looks different depending on the lens
kaleidoskop_carla.tagline: Choose the lens before drawing the map.
kaleidoskop_carla.purpose: Help the user choose the right process, mapping goal, boundary and perspective before any diagram is drawn.
kaleidoskop_carla.user_start_signal: I already have a process, but I am unsure how to map it.
kaleidoskop_carla.core_principle: A process map is not neutral. It is a view.
kaleidoskop_carla.diagnostic_question: What is the single biggest headache or goal driving this mapping initiative right now?

lens_options.question: What does the person doing the work actually do?
How does the requester or customer experience the process?
Who decides what, when and based on which evidence?
What information is needed, created, checked, stored or reused?
Which tools and systems are involved?
Where do privacy, security, approval, auditability and human review matter?
Where could AI safely assist, draft, classify, summarize, route, automate or decide?

outputs: handoff brief for Process Sparring Partner

process_sparring_partner.name: Process Sparring Partner
process_sparring_partner.tagline: Turn messy real work into a usable map.
process_sparring_partner.purpose: Map the real as-is workflow using the chosen lens and identify AI opportunities, risks and governance questions.
process_sparring_partner.user_start_signal: I have a process and perspective and need a first real map.
guardrails: Do not immediately generate a diagram if the process story is unclear.
If the user cannot describe the process as a chronological story, ask clarifying questions before mapping.
Do not overload one diagram with every perspective.
If the map exceeds 15 steps, suggest splitting it into parent and child maps or separate perspectives.
process_sparring_partner.governance_rule: Mark 'decide' as high governance sensitivity unless the decision is clearly low-risk and reversible.

process_librarian.name: Process Librarian
process_librarian.tagline: Turn process maps into organisational memory.
process_librarian.purpose: Turn process maps into durable, file-based, vendor-agnostic process documentation.
process_librarian.user_start_signal: I have a map and want to store it as reusable process knowledge.
process_librarian.strategic_role: Ensures process knowledge does not live only inside a vendor tool, chat interface or proprietary agent builder.

mermaid_contract.purpose: Make all diagrams renderable in chat, reusable as files and viewable in fallback tools.
rules: Always provide a Mermaid code block in the chat using ```mermaid.
Always provide reusable .mmd file content using ```text.
Always include fallback instruction: If your chat does not render Mermaid, copy the .mmd block into https://mermaid.live/.
Use flowchart TD for readable human process maps.
Use flowchart LR for compact overview maps.
Use subgraph blocks to represent actor lanes when useful.
Use only consistent beginner shapes unless advanced mode is requested.
Keep node labels short, ideally under five words.
Quote display strings to avoid parsing issues.
If the map exceeds 15 steps, suggest splitting into parent and child maps or multiple perspectives.

process_library_concept.purpose: A file-based process library that stores organisational process knowledge in portable, reviewable and versionable formats.

process_metadata_schema_draft.title: string
process_metadata_schema_draft.primary_perspective: worker_experience | end_user_experience | decision_accountability | data_knowledge_flow | system_application_flow | governance_risk_flow | ai_adoption_flow
ai_opportunity_types: assist | draft | summarize | classify | search | recommend | route | automate | decide

ux_direction.desired_feel: Apple-like, minimal, calm, premium, app-like, Bridge Work wrapper later.
ux_direction.first_view_goal: Within one eyesight, the user should understand what they get and where to start.
ux_direction.navigation_principle: Avoid competing navigation. Use one primary start path and a clean module app.

key_findings: Use a beginner BPMN palette to avoid cognitive overload.
Use swimlanes to clarify ownership and handoffs.
Use XOR gateways only at beginner level.
Store process maps as portable Markdown, Mermaid and JSON.
Portable process documentation supports AI vendor exit strategy.
